openings.claim: Unreliable storage addresses may drive delays. Preserve surname shelving but update the exception locator whenever books move, tied to the reserving reader; cart retention may remain useful.
openings.discriminator: Accurate addresses should reduce second-location searches at matched volume, book size and desk load. Persistently slow verified-location pickups dominated by waiting support the peak-demand rival.
openings.probe: Compare comparable pickups before/during updates using existing paper and timing sheet: arrival, service start, retrieval, completion, address accuracy and second searches. Verify recipient at handoff; record update work.
openings.uncertainty: Fit covers the capped probe only. Accurate reservation identity access and sustained feasibility are unconfirmed. Cart advantage may disappear after matching volume/size; peak demand may dominate.

openings.claim: Normalize shelf placement to the reservation holder surname within existing divider-card regions, strengthening search narrowing without another location-recording mechanism.
openings.discriminator: Fewer second-region searches and shorter shelf retrievals support household misfiling as a contributor. Unchanged searches after confirmed corrections defeat benefit; changing locations and peak demand remain rivals.
openings.probe: Compare dry retrievals before/after correcting identified household misfilings with existing cards, paper and timing sheet; perform no experimental handoffs.
openings.uncertainty: Reservation-holder records may be inadequate. Routine preparation used eight minutes, leaving two for useful corrections/probes. Cart retrieval and changed-location delays need not improve.

lineage.reason: Preserves current-locator repair, cart counterexample and demand rival.
Preserves narrower surname correction and retrieval-only test.

decision: Both are untested proposals from synthetic stipulations. Use only the evening clerk, two shelves and one cart; keep names/contact details behind the desk. Cap all preparation, corrections and probe work at ten clerk-minutes; stop at the cap. Neither establishes 95% available pickups within two minutes or zero wrong-reader handoffs. Interview representativeness and effects on reader uncertainty remain unknown.
